extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of Renaissance art and art history; painters and connoisseurs assessing or commissioning works
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative observations for judging Italian Renaissance paintings, frescoes, medals, and decorative schemes, including technique, composition, colour, portraiture, and material durability. Drawn from biographical/critical discussion of individual masters and works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelike portraiture / 'portraits from the life'
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and portraits should be drawn from life so they appear alive and truthful; many works praised here are 'full of portraits from the life' and contain 'portraits from life' of patrons and notable persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use living models for heads and faces to achieve naturalism and convincing likeness; include portraits of patrons where appropriate (e.g., cardinals portrayed in chapels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fine and lively colours and tasteful ornamentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Works praised for being 'painted with the finest and most lively colours, and wrought with various ornaments of gold', implying high value placed on vivid colouring and judicious ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ rich, lively colour harmonies and tasteful gold ornament where it enhances the work; excessive or vulgar ornament should be avoided (see anti-pattern on gilt relief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid crude gilt relief and showy ornament as a substitute for artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Gilded relief ornaments made to satisfy viewers with little understanding are criticised as 'a most barbarous thing in painting.' Bernardino's use of gilt relief is presented as an anti-pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on applied gilt relief or gaudy surface effects to mask deficiencies in drawing, composition, or colour; ornament should serve artistic ends, not merely dazzle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct spatial hierarchy — foreground should recede/proceed properly
rubrics_metrics.description: A grave error is described where painted relief and foreground treatment cause background architecture to appear more prominent than foreground figures: 'the things that should recede stand out more prominently than those that should strike the eye as the larger--a very grave heresy in our art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain convincing recession and proportion: foreground figures must read larger/prominent relative to background elements; perspective and modelling must support intended spatial relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice and mastery of medium (oil, distemper, fresco, stucco)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text discusses transitions and preferences among media—oil brought new colouring possibilities; many worked in distemper earlier; fresco and stucco require different technical mastery (and bad stucco work ruins decoration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the medium that suits the work and ensure mastery of its technical demands: oil for rich colour and subtle modelling, fresco for durable mural narrative, and properly executed stucco for ornament—avoid unskilled stucco that will ruin ornament over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish and workmanship depth versus rapid delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Finishing and quick delivery pleased patrons: 'he finished and delivered his works quickly, which is their pleasure, although such works are perchance less excellent than those that are made slowly and deliberately.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance timeliness with quality: faster execution can satisfy patrons but often at cost to excellence; be explicit about trade-offs when working to commissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical accuracy and expressive physiognomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for accurate, expressive depiction of bodies and faces (e.g., S. Jerome shown 'old, lean, and emaciated' like an anatomical model; angels and grieving figures portrayed with natural emotion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study anatomy and expressive physiognomy so figures convey age, emotion, and physical reality; careful modelling of features enhances verisimilitude and pathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness and originality in composition and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are commended for invention as well as colouring (Francia's Nativity: 'the invention and the colouring are worthy of nothing but praise').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for inventive narrative compositions and original solutions to subject-matter; novelty in conception is a valued component of excellence alongside technical execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative clarity in storytelling scenes (lives, miracles, histories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes from saints' lives and historic episodes are described in detail and valued for clear storytelling (e.g., stories of S. Ercolano, Miracles, campaign scenes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose narrative scenes so actions/readings are readily intelligible: clear sequencing, recognizable gestures, and descriptive detail (inscriptions can aid comprehension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of inscriptions to explain depicted scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Below each scene in one library is 'a Latin inscription, which describes what is contained therein,' suggesting inscriptions are part of an effective program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide textual labels or inscriptions where necessary to clarify iconography or identify persons/events, especially in complex cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of contemporary persons/patrons into sacred imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of portraying living persons as sacred figures (e.g., Signora Giulia Farnese as Madonna; portraits of popes and patrons included in religious scenes) indicate this was a practiced convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting patrons or contemporaries within sacred subjects, do so with sensitivity to decorum and clarity of role (donor portrait vs principal sacred figure), acknowledging both devotional and commemorative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill in small-scale and applied arts (medals, dies, niello)
rubrics_metrics.description: Francia's excellence as a goldsmith and die-maker is emphasised: making lifelike heads on medals and fine niello work is a distinct evaluative standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate high-relief modelling, portrait likeness, and fine detail in small-scale works; mastery of these techniques is a respected measure of craftsmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landscape detail and novel cityscapes (Flemish manner)
rubrics_metrics.description: A loggia was painted 'full of landscapes, depicting therein Rome, Milan, Genoa, Florence, Venice, and Naples, after the manner of the Flemings,' noted as unusual and satisfying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include carefully observed landscape or urban views and detailed backgrounds when appropriate; novel or learned landscape manners (e.g., Flemish detail) can increase a work's appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and fidelity in natural subjects (animals, foliage, plumage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Francia's caparisons with a 'vast forest of trees... great numbers of all sorts of animals... diversity of foliage and variety of branches' are praised for time spent on detailed natural depiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in accurate and varied rendering of flora and fauna where they form an important part of composition; variety and fidelity to nature are markers of virtuosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superficial execution; value deliberate labour
rubrics_metrics.description: Many works are dismissed as 'of no great excellence, and wrought in a superficial manner'; the author values slow, deliberate work for greater excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer careful, well-considered workmanship over hurried superficiality; depth of finish and thoughtful execution contribute substantially to artistic merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace of gesture and compositional refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific details such as an angel 'who has his hands clasped with such grace' are singled out as evidence of heavenly or refined workmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure gestures and small compositional details convey grace and appropriateness; delicate handling of hands, posture, and interaction heightens the work's refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability of materials and techniques (technical longevity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ornaments and stucco in some papal apartments 'are for the most part ruined' because the then-known stucco methods were inadequate, stressing the importance of durable technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select proven materials and methods for long-term survival of decorative work; technical innovation must be matched by durability to avoid premature ruin.
